value: Significant between-group differences in GMV were found in the right amygdala and left insula. The PTSD group had lower GMV in these structures compared with the TENP group, with the NEC group not being different from either group. value: Mean diffusivity significantly differed between groups in the right amygdala: both the PTSD and TENP groups had higher MD than NEC, with no difference between the sexually assaulted subgroups. No between-group differences were found in mean MD of the other ROIs.

FA significantly differed between groups in the right amygdala and bilateral ACC. Compared with NEC, both the PTSD and TENP groups had lower FA in the right amygdala and higher FA in the bilateral ACC, with no difference between the sexually assaulted subgroups. The TENP group had higher FA in the right insula than the PTSD group and a trend toward higher FA than NEC. No differences were found in the remaining ROIs.

The findings indicate microstructural differences in both traumatized groups compared with NEC, including higher MD and lower FA in the right amygdala and higher FA in the ACC bilaterally, as well as higher right-insula FA in TENP compared with PTSD.

value: Among trauma-exposed participants, PTSD severity was negatively correlated with GMV of the bilateral amygdala and insula. PTSD severity was also negatively correlated with FA and positively correlated with MD of the left hippocampus. No other significant correlations were observed.
These findings suggest that PTSD symptom severity is associated with macrostructural characteristics of the amygdala and insula and with microstructural characteristics of the left hippocampus.
